rows: Why does continental crust have so much K and U?
Highly incompatible elements; billions of years of partial melting extract them preferentially into the melt → accumulate in crust
What is the Eu anomaly and what causes it?
Deficit or excess in Eu relative to neighboring REE; caused by plagioclase fractionation (Eu²⁺ substitutes in plagioclase); negative Eu = plagioclase fractionated out
What is the Nb-Ta depletion signature?
Deficit of Nb and Ta relative to neighboring elements in spider diagrams; diagnostic of arc/subduction magmas; HFSE retained in subducted slab while LILEs fluid-mobilized
It has had partial melts extracted (which went to form crust), removing incompatible elements; residue is depleted relative to primitive mantle
MORB = Mid-Ocean Ridge Basalt (depleted mantle source, flat REE); OIB = Ocean Island Basalt (plume, enriched source, steep REE)
Sr-Nd-Pb radiogenic isotope ratios record time-integrated parent/daughter element fractionation; different domains = different histories
What is the iron peak in cosmic abundances?
⁵⁶Fe has the highest binding energy per nucleon → most stable nucleus → stellar nuclear burning converges toward Fe → peak in cosmic abundances at Z=26
